text:
aya: Quick blocker on docs PR #2633 — migration guide refers to \`cache_key_scope\` but doesn't say whether keys are namespaced per-tenant or global. Reviewers need explicit sentence.

liam: what's current runtime behavior?

runtime-bot: behavior: cache keys are namespaced by tenant id by default (so "user:123:key" for tenant A is isolated from tenant B). Optionally, private deployments can disable tenant namespacing via `cache.namespace=false` but that's not recommended unless you have an explicit multi-tenant overlay.

aya: do SDKs need to include tenant id when calling prefetch/get, or is that injected by auth?

runtime-bot: auth injects tenant scope server-side. SDKs should call cache APIs with logical keys (e.g., "user:123:prompt:abcd") and the server will prepend tenant namespace automatically. Do not manually prefix tenant id in SDK keys — doing so will double-namespace and cause misses.

docs-reviewer-nora: please add a one-line warning and a tiny JS snippet showing correct usage. Also clarify that tenant namespace is not encrypted — it's just a prefix for isolation.

aya: adding snippet now. Example: 
```javascript
// correct: pass logical key, runtime injects tenant namespace
client.cache.prefetch('user:123:prompt:abcd', payload, ttl=60)
// wrong: don't include tenant id yourself -> will be double-namespaced
client.cache.prefetch('tenant:acme:user:123:prompt:abcd', payload)
```

ci-bot: docs-preview: linkcheck passed, linter flagged missing warning callout.

aya: added callout: "Warning: do not manually prefix tenant IDs in cache keys. The server handles tenant scoping; manual prefixes can lead to hard-to-debug cache misses." Pushed.

docs-reviewer-nora: re-reviewing. Looks good; approve after CI green.

ci-bot: docs-preview: all checks passed.

docs-reviewer-nora: approved. merge when ready.

aya: merging now. thanks everyone!

runtime-bot: note: we will not change tenant namespacing behavior this release; changes require ops and security review.
